gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 identifies the same boundary flux consistency term in the mesh-dependent norm, applies the cut-trace/interpolation estimates to that term, and shows that the proof yields h^(2r-2) rather than the advertised h^(2r), including loss of the lowest-order convergence guarantee.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries diagnose the unsupported optimal-order theorem caused by the weakly imposed flux-boundary trace term: the h^{-1} boundary contribution is only controlled at order h^(2r-2), so the norm error is O(h^(r-1)) and the claimed h^(2r) squared estimate fails for nonempty Gamma_u.

component_coverage.gold_component: The h^{-1} flux-boundary contribution in the squared mesh-dependent norm is controlled by the cut-trace/interpolation argument only at O(h^(2r-2)), causing a one-power loss in the norm and removing the lowest-order Raviart–Thomas convergence guarantee for nonempty Gamma_u.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly computes the boundary-term scaling as h^(2r-2), translates it to an O(h^(r-1)) norm estimate, notes the r=1 O(1) case and r=0 trace problem, and connects this to failure of the stated optimal-order theorem and its needed qualification.
